thread:
Sam: quick async — pushed the kernel priming change to 10% canary at 09:15 UTC. Main wins: adaptive batch sizing cut tail p95 on short sequences by ~12%. Still seeing slot-steal spikes on 2 shards, need eyes. bench run id: bench/priming/4378.

Maria: nice! do you have the shard ids and a log snippet?

Sam: shard ids are eu-1b and us-west-3c. log excerpt below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T09:16:02Z] shard=eu-1b event=slot_steal rate=1.72% p95=48ms -> 42ms after priming
[2026-03-18T09:16:07Z] shard=us-west-3c event=slot_steal rate=2.10% p95=110ms -> 97ms after priming
```

Raj: thanks — that second p95 still high. any OOMs or retries?

Sam: no OOMs in the canary group, a handful of 500s (~6 total) correlated with a microburst on us-west-3c. not infra OOM, looks like queue saturation due to slot handoff timing.

Tess: I can take a look at the eviction TTLs this afternoon. my hunch: aggressive prefetch plus longer KV TTL is causing uneven slot occupancy. @Sam can you link the priming config you used?

Sam: config snippet: 
```yaml
priming:
  enabled: true
  initial_batch_target: 16
  adaptive_window_ms: 20
  kv_prefetch: true
  kv_ttl_seconds: 180
```
Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2198

ci-bot: build passed — runtime-e2e #3721 (bench/priming/4378). artifacts: logs.tar.gz

Maria: pinging @Oliver for kernel batching heuristics — any quick ideas for reducing slot handoff noise without raising user latency? maybe smoother ramp for adaptive batches?

Oliver: we could add a tiny jitter to batch boundary alignment and a hard cap on microburst batch sizes. ideological: prefer smoothing over hard caps so p50 unaffected. can prototype a 10% jitter.

Raj: also want to see the perf bench numbers across token lengths. any CSVs?

Sam: uploaded results to S3: s3://redwood-bench/priming/4378/results.csv. quick summary: p50 down 6%, p95 down 12% for seq<=128; seq>512 p95 unchanged.

Tess: i'll test TTL 90s vs 180s and run a small canary against eu-1b. will post findings in this thread.

Maria: follow-up ask — can we add a lightweight trace tag to requests hitting primed slots so we can filter traces easily? small PR would help debugging.

Sam: agree — will open a tiny PR for request tag (runtime:primed=true). aiming to have it up by EOD.

Oliver: FYI i'm OOO mid-afternoon but can review small PRs.

Tess: quick blocker — need a creds key to pull bench artifacts from s3 for the canary. @Raj can you share temporary read role?

Raj: granted role bench-read-temp to Tess, expires in 6 hours. LMK if you need extension.

Sam: thanks everyone. next steps: Tess runs TTL test, Oliver prototype jitter, Sam opens trace-tag PR, monitor canary for 4h then consider ramp to 30% if slot-steal <1.0%.

Maria: sounds good. :thumbsup:
